newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala says considering declassifying shares.
newsitem.headline: Ayala says considering declassifying shares.

text.p: Philippine conglomerate Ayala Corp is considering declassifying its A and B shares into common shares to remove the price discrepancy between the two types of shares.

Ayala president Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala II told stockholders the Philippine Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested declassification of the shares to prevent arbitraging between the A and B scrips.
"Based on that request ... We are looking at it. We have not made a decision at this time, but we are looking at it," he said.
Philippine listed companies used to offer A and B shares. A shares were exclusively for Filipino investors.
On Friday, Ayala A shares closed 25 centavos higher at 24 pesos, while its B shares ended 25 centavos down at 23.75 pesos.
